description.narrative: Phase V of TLPDP is implemented by the Australian Federal Police and continues long-standing support to the PNTL (Timor-Leste's Police Force) to institutionalise community policing in Timor-Leste and support the PNTL to ensure essential policing services continue.

organisation.narrative: Australia - Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade

description.narrative: TLPDP has provided specialised mariner training to 86 officers at Unidade Polisia Maritima (UPM) and equipped ten posts and two specialist teams with high powered binoculars and thermal imagers enhancing maritime security and surveillance capability. This has resulted in successful disruptions to people smuggling ventures and enabled investigation of damage to the Timor-Leste South Submarine Cable. Funding limitations precluded support for vessel procurement. However, in 2024, UPM acquired six response vessels and TLPDP provided specialist law enforcement mariner training to enable safe operation of these vessels. Additionally, TLPDP coordinated relationships between Australian Border Force and PNTL, to enable provision of outboard motors, personal floatation devices and surveillance drones to assist UPM to protect Timor-Leste’s national security. ‍ TLPDP completed a Maritime Review of PNTL UPM’s current operational status and the opportunities that exist for further maritime assistance including seeking funding for two new vessels to enable quicker response times and extended maritime surveillance range. ‍ TLPDP also worked to build capacity on border security through land-based surveillance training to the PNTL’s specialist police with a specific focus on human trafficking.

TLPDP has supported their primary partner, the National Police of Timor-Leste (PNTL), to strengthen accountability and inclusion by: ‍ •Promoting law enforcement cooperation and the establishment of formal interagency coordination arrangements within the law and justice sector, including facilitation of a joint ministerial workshop with government and civil society stakeholders. ‍ •Partnering with the US Department of Defense to upgrade PNTL’s digital radio network, strengthen policing capability and supporting the Timorese Civil Protection Authority. Collaboration has contributed to improved HADR response and coordination and disaster/frontline skills in the PNTL. ‍ •Training PNTL in border security, Close Personal Protection and English training, contributing to ASEAN accession. ‍ •Baseline data collection for the PNTL 2024 Gender Strategy and ongoing analysis of PNTL crime data. ‍ •Technical advice to strengthen inclusion in police training curriculum, supporting PNTL’s application for accreditation as a ‘Superior Police Institute’ to enable future administration of diploma and degree courses. ‍ •Embedding planning and budget advisor into PNTL which has encouraged long-term financial sustainability and timely budget processes. ‍ •Introducing Live Scan technology with specialised training resulting in improved fingerprinting capability. ‍ •Grant funding to Fundasaun Mahein on recommendations in GBV and digital communication technologies to inform PNTL priorities.

With Timor-Leste Police Development Program support, the PNTL Maritime Policing Unit responds to Maritime Search and Rescue Events (SAR) approximately monthly and have supported PNTL to intercept smugglers smuggling illicit goods into Timor-Leste from Indonesia via the ocean. TLPDP is working to uplift the SAR capacity of PNTL to respond to UNCLO (United Nations Convention on Law of the Sea Safety of Life at Sea) convention requirements. During the 23-24 FY TLPDP provided the following mariner training: ‍ 2 x Coastal Boat Skipper Courses (2 x16 officers) ‍ 3 x Basic Nautical Navigation and Chart-Plotter Operator courses (3 x 16 officers) ‍ 1 x Search and Rescue On-scene Co-ordinator Course (16 officers) ‍ 1 x Marine Radio Operator Course (16 officers) ‍ 2 x Thermal Imager Operator Training Courses (2 x 12 officers) ‍ 5 x Monthly Maritime Training Workshops (5 x 12 officers)
